admissionSummary.course: Visit 1 · Oct 15: Post-acute rehab after hip fracture progressing; CHF volume status improved on furosemide with decreased edema; continuing PT/OT and diuretic therapy
admissionSummary.reason:
Patient admitted for post-acute rehab after hip fracture, now with concurrent CHF, legs less swollen and able to lie flat on furosemide.
• Hip fracture — post-acute rehab in progress
• CHF — legs less swollen, tolerating furosemide 20 mg daily, able to lie flat
• Diet and follow-up — low-salt diet continued, cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks

Hip Fracture — Post-Acute Rehabilitation

Status: Resident admitted for post-acute rehabilitation following hip fracture. Currently in active rehab program.

Current Management: Physical and occupational therapy as part of rehabilitation protocol.

Congestive Heart Failure

Assessment and Plan

Hip Fracture — Post-Acute Rehabilitation

Resident is in active post-acute rehabilitation following hip fracture. Will continue physical and occupational therapy as tolerated.

1. Continue rehabilitation program with physical and occupational therapy.

Congestive Heart Failure

Resident's volume status has improved on current diuretic therapy, with decreased lower-extremity edema and ability to lie flat. Will continue current management.

1. Continue furosemide 20 mg daily.
2. Continue low-sodium diet.
